cards.title: Validate a Gin JSON request
cards.explanation: Gin 1.12.0, Go 1.25+. A complete package returning an http.Handler; no listener is opened. ShouldBindJSON decodes and validates binding tags without writing a response, so the handler owns its stable 400 contract. Quantity accepts 1–10; empty item, absent quantity, malformed JSON and wrong types are rejected. Unknown JSON fields are accepted by Gin defaults; this is not a strict schema or persistence example.

cards.title: Pass Gin request cancellation to a lookup
cards.explanation: Gin 1.12.0. Supply a non-nil context-aware lookup that returns promptly on cancellation. Pass c.Request.Context(), rather than relying on Gin Context fallback settings. This synchronous handler creates no goroutines. Cancellation/deadline/upstream errors have explicit 408/504/502 policies; a disconnected client may never receive the response. Missing path segments use router 404 behavior.

cards.title: Validate a Chi route parameter
cards.explanation: Chi v5.5.0 (Go 1.24+), using net/http handlers. The nested route extracts a path parameter from request context, then rejects nonnumeric, zero, negative and overflow IDs. A missing path segment is a 404 and an unsupported method is a 405, rather than an input-validation 400. No database or listener is needed.

cards.title: Keep Chi middleware and cancellation in one request
cards.explanation: Chi v5.5.0. Register middleware before routes. Supply non-nil work that observes its context and releases its resources before returning; the router cannot forcibly stop uncooperative work. The response policy distinguishes cancellation, expired deadlines and upstream errors. In-process tests can check headers even for an already-canceled request; network delivery after disconnect is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Assert parse boundaries with Testify subtests
cards.explanation: Testify 1.12.1. Save this complete package in a _test.go file. require stops the current subtest after a prerequisite fails; assert records a failure and continues. Use require only in the test goroutine. Zero and negatives are valid integer syntax here, not a positive-domain validator. Invalid inputs assert wrapped error identity and diagnostic input without comparing unstable messages.

cards.title: Verify a Testify mock and recovery sequence
cards.explanation: Testify 1.12.1. Save as _test.go; Store is the consumer interface, StoreMock is the test double. Once limits each expected call; AssertExpectations detects missing calls and unexpected calls fail. This bounded retry is suitable only for an idempotent read, not arbitrary writes. Add separate tests for immediate success, empty values and persistent failure; no production service is contacted.
